MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 10, 2018

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by CHAIR
  MEDAWAR.
  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
  CHAIR MEDAWAR led the assembly in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.
  3.  ROLL CALL
  Commissioners Present:  Edler, Carman, Scott, Medawar, Zigrang, Schachter, Yoo
  Staff Members Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Associate Planner Thom,
  Administrative Assistant Corea
  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT MADE A MOTION, SECONDED BY COMMISSIONER YOO
  to,
  APPROVE THE CORRECTED MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING OF AUGUST 6, 2018.
  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.
  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS
  None
  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  A.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL RESOLUTIONS THAT ARE PRESENTED FOR THE
  CONSIDERATION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION ON TONIGHT’S AGENDA AND
  ALL SUCH RESOLUTIONS SHALL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,
  APPROVE ITEM 6-A
  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.
  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS
  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 28-17; APPLICANT: MR. GREG ANDRES; LOCATION
  27809 CONESTOGA DRIVE; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination
  for first and second story additions to an existing single-family home and to construct a
  second dwelling unit in the rear yard. A Minor Deviation is required to reduce the front
  yard area by no more than 10%. A second Minor Deviation is required to continue a legal
  nonconforming west side yard setback.
  Planning Director Wahba presented Planning Application No. 28-17. This item was heard
  in December 2017 and was revised to address neighborhood compatibility concerns.
  Planning Director Wahba provided an overview of the most significant changes to the
  design. Staff remains concerned with the bridge, which is included in this design and the
  architectural design, which still has Spanish design elements.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that staff recommends the Planning Commission deny
  PA-28-17.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR expressed his concern with approving a bridge and stated that it may
  set a precedent for future proposed projects.
  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if there have been any changes to the length or width of
  the bridge. Planning Director Wahba stated that his understanding is that it is the same
  as the originally proposed design.
  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR opened the public comment.
  Bijan Khaleeli, Architect, stated the few changes made to the plan and stated that the
  applicants would like to agree on a design that is mutually acceptable. Mr. Khaleeli
  summarized the changes to the overall design of the project. He also stated that the

Planning Commission Meeting Minutes,  1
September 10, 2018
   purpose of the bridge is to facilitate accessibility to the Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) and
  added that the bridge was slightly shortened.
  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked if the home will have an elevator since reference was
  made to ADA. Mr. Khaleeli stated that it has not been considered, however, a chair lift
  may be an option.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about inconsistencies with the statistics sheet and the
  plan. Mr. Khaleeli stated that the plan would take precedent and expressed the difficulty
  in getting accurate measurements, but will work with staff to make sure that everything is
  consistent and accurate.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if the bridge has been shortened or under-filled. Mr.
  Khaleeli stated that the bridge ends closer and added that privacy will not be an issue with
  this proposal.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about stone being added to the design and also asked
  about the glass and iron on the door. Mr. Khaleeli stated that the stone would be a nice
  addition to the design and the front door was a special feature to have as well as client
  preference.
  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked if there is a view of the front of the house since the
  grade of this property is not flat. Mr. Khaleeli stated no.
  GREG ANDRES, Property Owner, stated that they have worked with the architect to make
  the design more of a ranch-style. He stated that he went to every one of the homeowners
  and HOA and all stated that they approve of the design including the bridge. Mr. Andres
  stated that there is no privacy issue, there are a lot of trees and vegetation which would
  block views to neighbor’s back yards. Mr. Andres stated that the purpose of the ADU is to
  bring his parents to move here from Chicago since the weather has caused them to have
  health issues. The proposal of the bridge would help his mother access from the main
  home to the ADU. Mr. Andres stated that his parents would be a big help to have in the
  care of their children since him and his wife work full-time. Mr. Andres stated that he plans
  to install a chair lift and added that in his profession he customizes homes to be ADA
  compliant.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that he applauds Mr. Andres for taking care of his parents,
  however, decisions must be made according to policy and stated that he would like to hear
  from the Planning Commission on recommendations for this project.
  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if there are any plans to make this home an assisted
  living/elder care facility in the future. Mr. Andres stated that this is not something that
  would be feasible due to the slope on the property.
  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if there have been any consideration to bring the ADU
  closer to the main house. Mr. Andres stated that due to the amount of grading that would
  be needed, this would be difficult.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that there was strong opposition to the bridge
  back in December and asked if other options were discussed. Mr. Andres stated that he
  was not aware of strong opposition to the bridge.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about the stone. Mr. Andres stated that if the
  stone was installed, it would look almost identical to his neighbors’ home and is willing to
  add this to the design.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR closed the public comment.
  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG commented that he likes the craftsman feel of the design.
  There are some inconsistencies with the windows but can easily be fixed. The stone
  would finish the design nicely. COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that he was opposed
  to the bridge due to it being so different than anything that has been presented and is still
  unsure about it. COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked about making the home bigger and
  building it into the hillside.
  COMMISSIONER YOO expressed his concern with the bridge and does not have an issue
  with the overall design. Homes in that area are not a consistent design and this design is
  not far removed from what is found in the neighborhood.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that the stone is needed to make it more of a
  ranch style. There needs to be consistency in what projects are being approved. There

Planning Commission Meeting Minutes,  2
September 10, 2018
   are still concerns with the bridge and approvals cannot be made due to particular
  situations as opposed to the effects on the whole community.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that the City Council has consistently preferred
  California Ranch Style or Western Ranch, however, in Larga Vista homes are a 50’s
  interpretation of Western Ranch. COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that the existing homes
  in the neighborhood influence the neighborhood compatibility. COMMISSIONER SCOTT
  stated that stone should be added to front of the house. He also added that with the
  statistics sheet and the changes as suggested, he would have no problem with the design.
  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that she is appreciative that there have been
  significant changes to make the design more compatible with the neighborhood. She
  stated that with the different roof lines terracing into the hillside, she is not confident how
  it will look and stated that there should be more consistency with the design of the
  windows, doors, and garage door, and added that stone would be helpful with
  compatibility.
  COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that the design has come a long way and agreed that
  stone should be added. He also stated that he is opposed to the bridge.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed concern with the divided lights.
  Planning Director Wahba stated this project may be approved without the bridge and
  provided suggestions for changes to the design. The applicant can be asked to forgo the
  arches. In regards to the divided lights, he stated that it is a common feature. There is
  also an option to continue this item.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if there are other bridges in residential homes in
  the city. Planning Director Wahba stated that there are one or two but do not read as a
  bridge from the street.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that there is still a need to go upstairs from the interior of
  the house to access the bridge to the ADU.
  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if it would be costly to build the ADU closer to the house.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that the ADU can be attached to the home and could be
  explored.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if the bridge is an issue or are they willing to move forward
  without the bridge. Mr. Khaleeli thanked the Planning Commission for their comments
  and stated that building into the hillside, aside the cost, would bring grading issues and
  require a retaining wall, which would add a significant delay to the project. Mr. Khaleeli
  requested a continuance in order to bring more information.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that this bridge cannot be seen from the street, if they
  had been proposing a deck to the back of the house, it would likely be approved.
  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that he is now in favor of the bridge.
  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that he would like staff to review this again
  especially with the states ruling on ADU’s. This may be the time to review the policy on
  properties similar to this one.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR suggested continuance of this item incorporating the changes as
  contributed by the Planning Commission.
  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if this will set a precedent. COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated
  that it is a Neighborhood Compatibility issue. There is little reason to think that this is a
  rental unit especially with the bridge in place. COMMISSIONER YOO stated that he is not
  sure if they have the jurisdiction to allow the bridge.
  A discussion ensued regarding approving the bridge.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion to, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  SCHACHTER to
  APPROVE PA-28-17, SUBJECT TO THE ACCURACY AND CONSISTENCY OF
  THE STATISTICS SHEET; ADDITION OF STONE DETAIL TO THE FRONT OF
  THE HOUSE TO STAFF’S SATISFACTION; CONSISTENCY OF DIVIDED
  LIGHTS; AND APPROVAL OF THE ACCESS DECK.

Planning Commission Meeting Minutes,  3
September 10, 2018
   AYES: EDLER, CARMAN, SCOTT, MEDAWAR, ZIGRANG, SCHACHTER
  NOES: YOO
  ABSTAIN:
  ABSENT:
  COMMISSIONER YOO stated that he is in support of the design and his objection is only
  in regards to the bridge and his authority in approving it in the back yard.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that there is a 20-day appeal period.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked staff to discuss any direction on bridges with the
  City Council in anticipation of any similar proposals.
  B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 12-18; APPLICANT: KALANI SCOYOC; LOCATION; 9
  BRANDING IRON LANE; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination to
  demolish the existing one-story home to construct a new two-story residence. A Minor
  Deviation is required for an increase of lot coverage by not more than 10%. A second
  Minor Deviation is required for the home to encroach into the required front yard by not
  more than 10%.
  Associate Planner Thom noted that a copy of a letter received today from a neighbor
  opposing the project has been provided to the Planning Commissioners. Associate
  Planner Thom provided a PowerPoint presentation and an overview of the proposed
  project.
  Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission
  approve this item with the conditions as provided by staff. She added that she went out
  to the property of the neighbor who is opposing the project and took photographs.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the Hawaiian Plantation style has ever been
  approved. Planning Director Wahba stated that this would be a first, but that is shares
  elements of other styles approved.
  Planning Director Wahba commented on staff’s perspective on the project.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT commented that the design has a lower roof that complies with
  the setback requirements today and will actually provide more light and air as compared
  to what is existing.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR opened the public comment
  Adria Sorensen, Sorenson Architects, provided a PowerPoint presentation highlighting
  their design process. She stated that the original design has been modified to fit in with
  the ranch style. Mrs. Sorenson stated that on the south elevation there are clear story
  windows. She added that a roof study and sun study was prepared; the sun study shows
  that there is no direct effect on the neighbors.
  Christopher Sorensen, Sorenson Architects, provided additional details on the design
  process and materials chosen for this design. Mr. Sorenson added that the existing ridge
  is large and that in the proposed design it will be lower, which will allow the neighbor to
  the south to enjoy more light than what she currently has. Mr. Sorenson stated that the
  proposed house along with various houses on the block will look similar in style as
  compared to the existing home. Mr. Sorenson commented that he believes that the
  proposed design is respectful of the neighborhood.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about the clear story windows on the second floor south
  side of the house. Mr. Sorenson stated that they were informed that there may be privacy
  issues. The windows were revised to be higher in order to address the privacy concern.
  Anka Muhl, 7 Branding Iron Lane, a letter (received 9/10/2018) was read by Mr. Cremens
  on her behalf. Ms. Muhl stated that she is opposing the second floor due to the view from
  various windows in her home. Ms. Muhl added that the design is too modern and is not
  compatible with the homes in the neighborhood. Ms. Muhl commented that there is a
  balcony on the second floor that wraps around and believes there will be privacy issues.
  She also stated that she believes that there will be less light coming into her home and
  her home value will decrease.
  ROBERT MEDAWAR asked about the balcony in the rear of the home. Mr. Sorensen
  stated that it will not wrap around and will include a planter and hedge. Mr. Sorenson
  further explained how the design will look from Mrs. Muhl’s home.

Planning Commission Meeting Minutes,  4
September 10, 2018
   Pat Davis, 11 Branding Iron Lane, stated that she believes she is going to be most affected
  by this project since her home sits below the project and she already has a neighbor with
  a massive home next to her home. Mrs. Davis is opposed to the massiveness of the
  proposed property, has concern with the home being closer to her home, and stated that
  she does not have any issue with the design.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR closed the public comment.
  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that the design is well done, although a departure
  from other proposals but is confident in this design team considering other projects that
  they have done and is in support of the project.
  COMMISSIONER YOO commented that the design of the home seems to be compatible
  and meets the setback requirements. He added that he understands Mrs. Muhl’s
  concerns, but has no issue with the proposal.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that they have met all the code requirements and
  the minor deviations are not significant. He does have concern with neighborhood
  compatibility particularly in the style of the garage door.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that he prefers the garage doors to be more consistent with
  ranch style and diminish some of the stone work. He also asked that the applicant
  communicate with the neighbors and address privacy concerns that they have.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed his concern with the north facing window on the
  second story since it appears not to be a clear story window and recommends that the
  windows be obscure. He also commented that the plans do not show dimensions that are
  significant in reviewing the project. COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that this will be the
  third largest home on the street and it will be on a narrow lot. He also expressed concern
  with the center roof pitch on the front.
  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated her concern is with neighborhood compatibility and
  also stated that the garage door is too bold to be consistent with other homes in the
  neighborhood. There should not be an issue with the sun but the overall design seems a
  bit contemporary as compared to the other more traditional homes in the neighborhood.
  COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he likes the design and believes that there will be
  more sunlight to the neighbor to the north and is in support of the project as presented.
  Planning Director Wahba summarized the recommendations as stated by the Planning
  Commissioners.
  A discussion ensued regarding the garage door options, materials that will be used for this
  project, and balcony screening.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  ZIGRANG to,
  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 12-18 APPROVING THE MINOR
  DEVIATION FOR AN INCREASE OF LOT COVERAGE BY NOT MORE THAN
  10% AND A SECOND MINOR DEVIATION FOR THE ENCROACMENT OF THE
  PROPOSED RESIDENCE INTO THE REQUIRED FRONT YARD, SUBJECT TO
  APPROVAL OF THE GARAGE DOOR TO THE SATISFATION OF STAFF; THAT
  THE BATHROOM WINDOW ON THE SECOND STORY NORTH ELEVATION BE
  OBSCURE; THAT 5’ BALCONY SCREENS ON THE NORTH AND SOUTH SIDES
  BE INSTALLED AND MAINTAINED.
  AYES: EDLER, CARMAN, SCOTT, MEDAWAR, ZIGRANG, SCHACHTER, YOO
  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:
  ABSENT:
  Planning Director Wahba stated there is a 20-day appeal period.
  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 11-18; APPLICANT: ROLLING HILLS VILLAS HOA;
  LOCATION: 901 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE; An amendment to City Council Resolution No.
  2054 (PA-15-03), requesting a Variance to eliminate the hiking trail on the hillside behind
  the condominiums located at 901 Deep Valley Drive.

Planning Commission Meeting Minutes,  5
September 10, 2018
   Planning Director Wahba began by clarifying that this is a private trail for the use of the
  residents of 901 Deep Valley Drive, a 55 year and older assisted living building. Planning
  Director Wahba presented a PowerPoint presentation on Planning Application No. 11-18
  and summarized the staff report.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission
  approve Resolution No. 11-18, granting an amendment to City Council Resolution No.
  2054, granting a Variance for a reduction of open space required per dwelling unit as
  required under Section 17.37.040 (C) of the RHEMC, and removing the hillside trail from
  the project’s required open space.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR opened the public hearing.
  Rick Jones, President, Rolling Hills Villas HOA stated that the trail is a severe hazard to
  the residents and guests due to its steep slope. Mr. Jones stated that aside from the
  hillside being steep, there may also be a coyote den near the trail. Mr. Jones stated that
  he spoke to the HOA board and they agreed that they would like that the trail be off limits
  to residents and guests.
  ROBERT SCHACHTER asked how the entrance to the trail will be closed off. Mr. Jones
  stated that signage will be posted.
  In response to a question by CHAIR MEDAWAR, Mr. Jones stated that the trail is only
  cleared of brush by the Fire Department once a year.
  Lesa Barker, 901 Deep Valley Drive, stated that during their search for a home in the area,
  her and her husband were informed that there was a trail behind the building and impacted
  their decision to purchase a unit in the building. When she attempted to use the trail, it
  was impassable. Mrs. Barker read a portion of a letter posted for property owners in the
  building, which stated that the trail was a selling feature and one of the reasons that they
  would like to close it had to do with cost, and stated that the letter also mentioned concerns
  about coyotes. Mrs. Barker expressed her concern with the validity of the various concerns
  with the trail. She also commented that her husband was never approached about the
  maintenance issues with the trail and stated that she believes it is a cost issue and not a
  liability issue. She has attempted to deal with the HOA president without success.
  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if the HOA made a determination and went through their
  voting process to make this request. Planning Director Wahba stated that yes, the request
  came from the board.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR closed the public hearing.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that the trail will still remain accessible for the fire
  personnel and for annual brush maintenance. Signs could be posted and fencing could
  be installed to prevent people from using it.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER questioned if the trail was used in order for the original
  project to be approved to meet the open space per unit requirement. Planning Director
  Wahba stated that this was the case.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER expressed concern with changing a CUP and other
  requests to follow.
  A discussion ensued regarding the decision to approve this amendment.
  COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT to,
  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 11-18, AN AMENDMENT TO CITY
  COUNCIL RESOLUTION NO. 2054, GRANTING A VARIANCE FOR A
  REDUCTION OF OPEN SPACE REQUIRED PER DWELLING UNIT AS
  REQUIRED UNDER SECTION 17.37.040 (C) OF THE RHEMC, AND REMOVING
  THE HILLSIDE TRAIL FROM THE PROJECT’S REQUIRED OPEN SPACE.
  AYES: EDLER, SCOTT
  NOES: CARMAN, MEDAWAR, ZIGRANG, SCHACHTER, YOO
  ABSTAIN:
  ABSENT:
  Planning Director Wahba stated that there is a 20-day appeal period.

Planning Commission Meeting Minutes,  6
September 10, 2018
   9.  COMMISSION ITEMS
  Per the request of CHAIR MEDAWAR, Planning Director Wahba provided a brief update
  on the CalWater Pipeline Project.
  10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS
  Planning Director Wahba reminded the Planning Commission that there is a General Plan
  Advisory Committee Meeting on Thursday, September 20th at 6:00 p.m. and a Joint City
  Council and Planning Commission meeting on Tuesday, October 9, 2018 to discuss the
  General Plan Update.
  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION
  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, AUGUST 14, 2018
  B.  DRAFT MINUTES OF THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION, AUGUST 20, 2018
  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved to
  receive and file Items 11A and 11B.
  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.
  12.  ADJOURNMENT
  CHAIR MEDAWAR adjourned the meeting at 10:20 p.m. The next Planning Commission
  meeting will be held on Monday, October 1, 2018 at 7:00 p.m.
